  "text": "When the bakery closed, Nina found a bicycle leaning against the flour bins in the yard. A paper bag covered the saddle.

Her father stood beside it, working the bell with his thumb. It made a dry click.

“Cable’s gone,” he said.

“Bells don’t have cables.”

“This one might.”

She put the empty bread trays against the wall.

The bicycle had been blue when she rode it to school. He had painted the frame green without removing the old registration sticker.

“You said you needed something for getting here.”

“I said the bus was expensive.”

He straightened the front wheel between his shoes.

“Same thing, more or less.”

Nina lifted the bag. The saddle had been patched with black tape, carefully overlapped.

“Does Mum know you brought it?”

“She found the pump.”

From inside came the scrape of a chair. Nina’s employer was counting the till.

“I can’t keep it in the flat.”

“There’s a bracket you can get. Goes on the wall.”

“The landlord won’t allow holes.”

Her father nodded. He pulled the bag back over the saddle.

Nina wheeled the bicycle across the yard and squeezed both brakes. The rear one caught slowly.

“Can you tighten that?”

He reached into his coat pocket. The spanner was already in his hand.

While he worked, she went inside and wrapped two unsold rolls in paper.

“Cheese,” she said, putting them in his bicycle basket.

He finished the adjustment and tested the wheel.

“Try it now.”

She rode to the gate, turned awkwardly, and came back with her feet off the pedals.

He moved the bread trays so she had room to stop."
